'''Kahlil Ameer''' "'''Kay'''" '''Felder Jr.''' (born March 29, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Victoria Libertas Pallacanestro|Victoria Libertas Pesaro]] of the [[Serie A2 (basketball)|Serie A2]]. Felder, a {{convert|5|ft|9|in|adj=on}} [[point guard]], declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]] at the conclusion of his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year at [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]], and was drafted in the second round. Felder is the [[Horizon League]] career [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s leader.

==High school career==
Felder attended [[Pershing High School]] in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]] where he was named [[Public School League]] MVP his senior season.<ref name="ou bio"/> His senior year, he finished fourth in [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]] voting.<ref name=nyt_article>{{cite news|first=Joanne C.|last=Gerstner|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/28/sports/ncaabasketball/kahlil-felder-oakland-university.html|title=Key Measure of a 5–9 College Star: 25.3 Points a Game|newspaper=The New York Times|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=February 11, 2016 }}</ref>

He was not heavily recruited by high-major colleges and was noticed by Oakland assistant coach [[Saddi Washington]].<ref name=nyt_article/> Felder was also recruited by [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]], [[Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball|Southern Illinois]] and [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Tony|last=Paul|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2016/02/09/kay-felder-oaklands-big-little-man/80081272/|title=Kay Felder is Oakland's big little man|newspaper=Detroit News|date=February 9, 2016|access-date=February 12, 2016}}</ref> Oakland offered Felder a scholarship when he was a sophomore and he committed prior to his senior season. To show their commitment to him, Oakland did not recruit a [[point guard]] the season before he arrived so Felder knew there would be no competition.<ref name=espn_article/>

==College career==
[[File:Felder dribbling (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Felder with Oakland University in 2014]]
In 2013–14, Felder was named the [[Horizon League]] Freshman of the Year.<ref name=espn_article/> As a sophomore in 2014–15, Felder finished second in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) with 7.6 assists per game,<ref name="ou bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.goldengrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kay_felder_849265.html|title=20 Kay Felder|publisher=Oakland University|access-date=February 11, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010205044/http://www.goldengrizzlies.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kay_felder_849265.html|archive-date=October 10, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> two assists behind the leader, [[Jalan West]] of [[Northwestern State Demons basketball|Northwestern State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/seasons/2015-leaders.html|title=2014–15 Leaders|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|access-date=February 17, 2016}}</ref> He was also a finalist for the [[Lou Henson Award]], given to the "Mid-Major Player of the Year".<ref name="lute olson press release">{{cite web|url=http://www.luteolsonaward.com/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111042654/http://www.luteolsonaward.com/ |archive-date=January 11, 2016 |date=January 7, 2016 |access-date=February 11, 2016 |title=Mid-Season Player of Year Honors |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Junior year (2015–16)===
As a junior in 2015–16, Felder was consistently being evaluated as an [[NBA]] prospect, with professional scouts having attended Oakland's games.<ref name=nyt_article/><ref name=espn_article>{{cite web|first=Myron|last=Medcalf|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14704838|title=Kahlil Felder might be only 5-foot-9, but he could do something unprecedented in college basketball|date=February 4, 2016|access-date=February 12, 2016|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> In December, playing against [[2015–16 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]], then-No. 1 [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]], and then-No. 5 [[2015–16 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], Felder averaged 35 points, 7 assists and made 47.9% of his field goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kahlil-felder-1/gamelog/2016/|title=Kay Felder 2015–16 Game Log|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=December 28, 2016}}</ref> Oakland led at halftime of each of those games, beating Washington, but losing to Michigan State and Virginia. Felder scored 37 points with nine assists against Michigan State in a 99–93 overtime loss at [[The Palace of Auburn Hills]].<ref name=nyt_article/>

Felder was named a top-five finalist for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], given to the top male point guard in Division I.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoophall.com/news/2016/3/7/final-five-candidates-announced-for-2016-bob-cousy-award.html|title=Final Five Candidates Announced for 2016 Bob Cousy Award|date=March 7, 2016|access-date=March 7, 2016|publisher=Basketball Hall of Fame|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308061104/http://www.hoophall.com/news/2016/3/7/final-five-candidates-announced-for-2016-bob-cousy-award.html|archive-date=March 8, 2016}}</ref> He was also named the mid-season recipient of the [[Lute Olson Award]], given annually to the most outstanding non-freshman men's college basketball player in [[NCAA Division I]].<ref name="lute olson press release"/> He was placed on the mid-season watch list for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Terrence|last=Payne|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}}</ref>

Felder won the NCAA Player of the Week award on February 9, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/video/basketball-men/2016-02-09/mbk-mens-basketball-kay-felder-player-week|title=Men's Basketball: Kay Felder named Player of the Week|date=February 9, 2016|access-date=February 12, 2016|publisher=NCAA}}</ref> He also won six Horizon League Player of the Week awards during the season, tying the Horizon League record.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wxyz.com/sports/oakland-universitys-kay-felder-named-horizon-league-mens-player-of-the-week-for-6th-time|title=Oakland University's Kay Felder named Horizon League Men's Player of the Week for 6th time|publisher=WXYZ|date=February 15, 2016|access-date=February 17, 2016|archive-date=February 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160225091422/http://www.wxyz.com/sports/oakland-universitys-kay-felder-named-horizon-league-mens-player-of-the-week-for-6th-time|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Despite using only three of his four years of college eligibility, Felder broke the Horizon League career [[assist (basketball)|assists]] mark of 699, which was originally set by Ralph Lee of [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] in 1986.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/02/11/oaklands-felder-sets-horizon-assist-record-loss/80265954/|title=OU's Felder sets assist record in loss; UDM falls|agency=Associated Press|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=February 12, 2016|access-date=February 13, 2016}}</ref> Felder also set the Oakland school record for consecutive [[free throw]]s made, making 46 in a row with his last miss on January 29.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/article60543286.html |title=Oakland beats Wright State 89–73 for 2nd place in Horizon |agency=Associated Press |newspaper=The News Tribune |date=February 15, 2016 |access-date=February 17, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160225010330/http://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/article60543286.html |archive-date=February 25, 2016 }}</ref> Felder was named the [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Player of the Year]] and earned All-Horizon League First Team honors.<ref>{{cite news|first=James|last=Jahnke|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/03/01/horizon-league-basketball-kay-felder/81160582/|title=Horizon League basketball awards: OU's Kay Felder player of the year|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=March 1, 2016|access-date=March 1, 2016}}</ref>

On April 5, 2016, Felder declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Snyder|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/04/05/oaklands-kay-felder-leaving-nba-draft/82648850/|title=Oakland's Kay Felder declares for NBA draft|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 5, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cleveland Cavaliers (2016–2017)===
[[File:Tyler Johnson Heat 2016.jpg|thumb|right|Felder guards [[Tyler Johnson (basketball)|Tyler Johnson]] of the [[Miami Heat]] in 2016.]]
During the 2016 [[NBA Draft Combine]], the {{convert|5|ft|9|in|m|adj=on}} Felder tied [[Pat Connaughton]] for the second-highest maximum vertical leap recorded in draft combine history at {{convert|44|in|cm}}.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Snyder|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/05/12/kay-felder-nba-draft/84276038/|title=NBA draft combine: Oakland's Kay Felder living up to tall ambitions|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=May 13, 2016|access-date=May 13, 2016}}</ref> Despite his high marks in the draft combine, Felder was still projected to be a late-second-round draft pick, with the risk that he would perhaps not get drafted altogether. Felder was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the 54th overall pick. He was later traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on draft night,<ref>{{cite web|first=Lev|last=Facher|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2016/06/24/oakland-kay-felder-2016-nba-draft/86301806/|title=NBA draft: Oakland's Kay Felder goes in Round 2 to Cleveland|newspaper=Detroit Free Press|date=June 24, 2016}}</ref> and in July 2016, he joined the Cavaliers for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sykes |first=Joe |date=July 5, 2016 |title=Cavs Announce 2016 Samsung NBA Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/summer-league-roster-2016 |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On August 6, 2016, he signed a three-year, $2.4 million contract with the Cavaliers.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jirousek |first=Brandon |date=August 6, 2016 |title=Cavaliers Sign Kay Felder |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases/felder-160806 |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Manning |first=Chris |date=August 7, 2016 |title=Kay Felder's deal is for three-years [sic], $2.4 million |url=https://www.fearthesword.com/2016/8/7/12398602/kay-felder-deal-contract-information-cleveland-cavaliers |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=fearthesword.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the Cavaliers in their third game of the season on October 29, scoring two points in five minutes off the bench in a 105–99 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899479|title=LeBron James, Kyrie Irving lead Cavaliers past Magic, 105–99|work=ESPN.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}}</ref> On December 14, with [[Kyrie Irving]] resting, Felder scored a season-high 14 in 23 minutes in a 93–85 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899821|title=With Big Three taking night off, Cavaliers lose 93–85 to Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}}</ref> During his rookie season, he had multiple [[Assignment (NBA D-League)|assignments]] with the [[Canton Charge]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2016–17 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 6, 2017 |archive-date=June 28, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628000000/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 14, 2017, Felder was traded, along with [[Richard Jefferson]], two future second-round draft picks and cash considerations, to the Atlanta Hawks in exchange for the rights to [[Sergiy Gladyr]] and [[Dimitrios Agravanis]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Nick |date=October 14, 2017 |title=Cavaliers Complete Trade with Atlanta |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/trade-171014 |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was immediately waived by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Meghan |date=October 14, 2017 |title=Hawks Acquire Draft Picks and Cash Considerations From Cavs |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-acquire-felder-and-jefferson |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2017)===
On October 16, 2017, Felder was claimed off waivers by the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web |date=October 16, 2017 |title=Bulls waive Jarell Eddie and Diamond Stone, claim Kay Felder |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-jarell-eddie-and-diamond-stone-claim-kay-felder |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was waived by the Bulls on December 19, 2017.<ref name="bulls-waive">{{cite web |date=December 19, 2017 |title=Bulls waive Kay Felder |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-kay-felder |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He appeared in 14 games for Chicago and averaged 3.9 points, 1.0 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 9.6 minutes. He also played in three games for the [[Windy City Bulls]] and averaged 17.3 points, 3.6 rebounds and 4.6 assists, while shooting 45.2 percent from the field (19-of-42).<ref name="bulls-waive"/>

===Detroit Pistons (2018)===
On January 15, 2018, Felder signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]], thus splitting his time between the Pistons and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Detroit Pistons|url=https://twitter.com/detroitpistons/status/953008893373894662|title=OFFICIAL: Pistons have signed Kay Felder|work=Twitter|date=January 15, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref>

===Raptors 905 (2018)===
On August 21, 2018, Felder signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Naje |first=B. |date=August 21, 2018 |title=Raptors Sign Kay Felder |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-kay-felder |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 12, 2018 Felder was waived by the Raptors, just before the start of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raptors Waive Four |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-waive-four |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 12, 2018 |date=October 12, 2018}}</ref> He was then added to the Raptors' G League affiliate, the [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Naje |first=B. |date=November 1, 2018 |title=Raptors 905 Announce Opening Day Roster |url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-announce-opening-day-roster/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204010307/https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-announce-opening-day-roster/ |archive-date=December 4, 2018 |access-date=November 1, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On December 3, 2018, Felder was waived by the Raptors 905 released after his arrest over a charge of domestic violence.<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Doug |date=December 3, 2018 |title=Raptors 905 waives Kay Felder after domestic violence charges |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/2018/12/03/raptors-905-waives-kay-felder-after-domestic-violence-charges.html |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=Toronto Star}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=December 3, 2018 |title=Raptors cut G League guard Kay Felder after domestic violence arrest |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25444109 |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

===Xinjiang Flying Tigers (2019–2020)===
On March 25, 2019, Felder signed with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=CBA club Xinjiang confirms signing of Felder to replace Adams|url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-03/25/c_137922669.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190602180216/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-03/25/c_137922669.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 2, 2019|website=Xinhua|access-date=June 2, 2019|date=March 25, 2019}}</ref> He was replaced by [[Ian Clark (basketball)|Ian Clark]] on January 14, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last=Xinhua |date=January 14, 2020 |title=Ian Clark returns to action for the CBA's Xinjiang Flying Tigers |url=https://www.chinadailyhk.com/article/118539 |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=ChinaDaily Hong Kong}}</ref>

===Zhejiang Guangsha Lions (2021)===
Felder joined the [[Zhejiang Guangsha Lions]] for the 2020–21 season. He averaged 13.1 points, 5.9 assists, 4.5 rebounds, and 1.8 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=OAKLAND TO THE NBA: KAY FELDER |url=https://goldengrizzlies.com/news/2021/8/3/mens-basketball-oakland-to-the-nba-kay-felder.aspx |website=[[Oakland Golden Grizzlies]] |access-date=December 24, 2021 |date=August 3, 2021}}</ref>

===Shanxi Loongs (2021–2023)===
In 2021, Felder signed with the [[Shanxi Loongs]] of the Chinese Basketball Association.<ref>{{cite news |title=Guangdong rallies past Shenzhen for 6th straight win, Xinjiang snaps skid |url=https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202110/29/WS617b443ba310cdd39bc72002.html |access-date=December 24, 2021 |work=[[China Daily]] |date=October 29, 2021}}</ref>

===Beijing Royal Fighters (2023–2024)===
In 2023, Felder joined the [[Beijing Royal Fighters]].<ref>{{cite web |title=欢迎格兰特·里勒、凯·费尔德和贾卡尔·桑普森加盟北控篮球俱乐部 |url=https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20231014A04RKR00 |publisher=腾讯新闻 |access-date=21 October 2024 |date=14 October 2023}}</ref>

===Nanjing Monkey Kings (2024)===
On October 21, 2024, Felder signed with [[Nanjing Monkey Kings]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |title=冲击季后赛不容有失，同曦官宣签下新外援 |url=https://www.yangtse.com/zncontent/4090837.html |publisher=扬子晚报/紫牛新闻 |access-date=21 October 2024 |date=21 October 2024}}</ref>

===Victoria Libertas Pesaro (2025–present)===
On September 7, 2025, he signed with [[Victoria Libertas Pallacanestro|Victoria Libertas Pesaro]] of the [[Serie A2 (basketball)|Serie A2]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kay-felder-signs-one-year-deal-with-vl-pesaro/|title=Kay Felder Signs One-Year Deal with VL Pesaro|last=|first=|date=September 7, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 7, 2025}}</ref>

Felder's father, Kahlil Felder Sr., played basketball at [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] from 1990 to 1992.<ref name=espn_article/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.emueagles.com/documents/2015/11/3//FullBook_FINAL_110315.pdf?id=4038|title=2015–16 Eastern Michigan men's basketball media guide|work=EMUEagles.com|publisher=Eastern Michigan University|access-date=February 13, 2016}}</ref> Felder is the cousin of former NBA player [[Steve Smith (basketball)|Steve Smith]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jill|last=Hudson|url=https://andscape.com/features/steve-smith-talks-preseason-basketball-and-his-journey-to-the-small-screen/|title=Steve Smith talks preseason basketball and his journey to the small screen|work=andscape.com|date=September 20, 2016|access-date=September 20, 2016}}</ref>
